methods.label: Replace division with multiplication
methods.explanation:
Dividing by the nonzero fraction \(3/5\) means multiplying by its reciprocal, \(5/3\). Thus, for any starting number \(x\), the two operations give
\[
\left(x\cdot\frac34\right)\div\frac35
=x\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac53
=x\cdot\frac54.
\]
The same effect is therefore multiplying by \(\boxed{\frac54}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
methods.levelReason: The reciprocal rule, fraction multiplication, and cancellation give a complete elementary solution. The argument also applies when the starting number is zero.

candidate.annotationRationale: The decisive target is interpreting fraction division as multiplication by a reciprocal. Fraction multiplication and reduction support finding the resulting single multiplier.

review.mathematicalCheck: Division by the nonzero fraction 3/5 multiplies by 5/3, so the combined multiplier is (3/4)(5/3)=5/4. No division by the starting number occurs, so zero is included.
review.levelCheck: The reciprocal rule and fraction cancellation are explained using elementary AMC 8 mathematics. The variable clearly represents an arbitrary starting number.
